Question B-003-013-002.

Why the correct answer is right: A transmitter set for half the repeater deviation will sound quiet because the receiver sees less frequency swing for the same speech.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Your audio will be low": This is the correct choice because a transmitter set for half the repeater deviation will sound quiet because the receiver sees less frequency swing for the same speech.
- sourceIndex 1: "Your audio will be distorted": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Your audio will be low. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "Your range will be shorter": This answer would fit a different fault than Your audio will be low. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "The repeater will not respond": This option confuses another station topic with Your audio will be low. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
